title: OKR Initiative Capacity & Entitlement Framework
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: As Redwood scales, teams repeatedly request additional initiative headroom mid-quarter which causes scope churn, missed OKR targets, and unclear trade-offs between reliability, platform, and new feature work. There is no formal capacity budgeting or entitlement model that ties company-level OKRs to cross-functional initiative allocations.

Objective: Define and pilot an "Initiative Capacity & Entitlement Framework" that (1) maps company-level OKRs to measurable initiative budgets (engineering hours, runway points, and infra dollars), (2) surfaces cross-functional dependencies early, and (3) provides a transparent approval and reallocation flow for mid-cycle changes.

Scope: This ticket covers framework design, stakeholder alignment, a lightweight tooling spec for tracking entitlements in the Console roadmap view, and a single-quarter pilot with 4 initiatives (runtime perf, Dedicated autoscaling, Console UX, and Private deployment onboarding). Implementation of enforcement (hard quotas) is out of scope for Q1 pilot — we will focus on visibility and process.

Approach:
- Build a simple allocation model: company OKRs get an entitlement pool split by initiative priority band (Core, Strategic, Exploratory). Each initiative maps to roles (ENG, PM, Design, SRE) and an estimated quarterly capacity slice (FTE-weeks and infra $).
- Create an approval flow (PM + Eng Lead + Finance) for initial allocations and any >15% reallocation mid-cycle.
- Add a Console-level UI spec (roadmap lane) to display entitlement vs. burn, with links to per-initiative rollout plans and cost dashboards.
- Pilot governance with a Steering Committee (VP Product, VP Engineering, Head of Platform) and run two arbitration sessions during the quarter.

Deliverables:
1) Framework spec document (Confluence)
2) Allocation spreadsheet template and example populated for pilot initiatives
3) Console roadmap mock and tracking columns (UI spec + data contract)
4) Pilot retro and recommendation (go/no-go for hard quota enforcement)

Why unique: This is intended to shift conversations from ad-hoc resourcing to outcome-aligned entitlements, preserving runway for reliability and platform investments while enabling predictable product delivery.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Steering Committee signs off on allocation model and approval flow.
2) Console roadmap mock created with clear data contract for at least two metrics (FTE-weeks burn, infra spend).
3) Pilot initiatives have baseline allocations and weekly burn reporting (minimum 6 weekly updates).
4) Pilot retro document with concrete recommendation and next-steps submitted by due_date.
metrics:
- Percent of initiatives with allocation vs. without (target: 100% for pilot set)
- Variance between allocated and actual FTE-weeks (target: <= 20%)
- Number of reallocation requests >15% (target: <= 2)
- Stakeholder satisfaction score from pilot survey (target: >= 4/5)
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (Weeks 1-2): Draft framework and allocation template. Align with Finance and People Ops.
Phase 2 (Weeks 3-4): Workshop with pilot initiative leads, finalize initial allocations. Build Console mock.
Phase 3 (Weeks 5-11): Run pilot; teams report weekly burn to shared dashboard; Steering Committee meets at week 7 and week 11 for arbitration.
Phase 4 (Week 12-13): Retro, finalize recommendation, and propose next-step tickets (enforcement tooling, scaling to org).
stakeholders:

Pilot leads: Liam O'Connor (Runtime), Maria Gonzales (Dedicated), Owen Marshall (Console UX), Asha Patel (PM lead).
Supporting: Finance (TBD), People Ops (TBD), Design System (Catherine Ng).
risks:
- Overhead: extra process may slow rapid-response work. Mitigation: pilot focuses on visibility not hard gating.
- Acceptance: teams may resist allocation constraints. Mitigation: include teams in allocation workshops and allow limited reallocation requests.
- Data fidelity: estimates for FTE-weeks are noisy. Mitigation: conservative default buffer and weekly burn updates.
